albums.blurb: Wave is the fifth studio album by the composer at the center of bossa nova, and his first for A&M's CTI imprint, produced by Creed Taylor and recorded at Rudy Van Gelder's New Jersey studio in 1967 with arrangements by Claus Ogerman. It is entirely instrumental — Jobim on piano, guitar, and harpsichord over a largely American band — and it introduced two instant standards, the title track and "Triste," alongside quieter miniatures like "Batidinha."
albums.reception: The album reached number 5 on Billboard's Jazz Albums chart and number 114 on the Billboard 200, and AllMusic's review singles out its "absolutely first-rate tunes — actually miniature tone poems" as the peak of the Jobim/Ogerman collaboration.

albums.blurb: PJ Morton is a New Orleans singer, songwriter, and keyboardist — the son of gospel bishop Paul S. Morton and, since 2012, the touring and studio keyboardist for Maroon 5. Gumbo is his fifth solo album and the first he self-released on his own Morton Records after walking away from a major-label deal; its live-band southern soul features BJ the Chicago Kid and the Hamiltones, and it was successful enough to spawn the symphonic live follow-up Gumbo Unplugged a year later.
albums.reception: Gumbo earned Morton two nominations at the 60th Grammy Awards, for Best R&B Album and, for the song "First Began," Best R&B Song.

albums.blurb: Air is the Versailles duo of Nicolas Godin and Jean-Benoît Dunckel, and Moon Safari is their debut, released on Source/Virgin in January 1998. Built on Moog, vocoder, Rhodes, and Wurlitzer, with American singer Beth Hirsch's vocals on "All I Need" and "You Make It Easy," its retro-futurist lounge-pop — led by the single "Sexy Boy" — helped carry the French electronic scene of the late nineties to British and American audiences alongside Daft Punk's Homework.
albums.reception: Moon Safari was met with wide critical praise on release and reached number 6 on the UK Albums Chart, selling around 600,000 copies in the UK alone.
